_comment: Animation scorecard limits (tools/anim/scorecard.py). Every limit is the approved Knight v2 clips' own extreme for that metric and clip kind plus the stated margin; 'other' is the envelope over the knight's kinds and applies to clip kinds the knight does not have. The knight is the sword_shield family; 'families' widens a limit for another design.json family only where its style needs the motion, each with its reason (it never narrows one, and never lifts the anatomical caps). Non-biped rigs are n/a for bend, limb speed and foot slide; a gait's foot slide needs the troop's booth gait speed. Regenerate with python tools/anim/scorecard.py --derive.

elbow_bend.how: maximum: knight per-kind max + 10 deg. Minimum: the anatomical cap -5 deg (no hyperextension), or the knight's own minimum where it goes further (its hits); a limb straighter than the knight's is a style, not a fault

knee_bend.how: maximum: knight per-kind max + 10 deg. Minimum: the anatomical cap -5 deg (no hyperextension), or the knight's own minimum where it goes further (its hits); a limb straighter than the knight's is a style, not a fault

ang_speed_arms.how: knight per-kind max x 1.25, never under 8 deg/100ms; death x 2.0 (a falling body flings its arms: the knight's deaths are its one style, other troops fall harder)

ang_speed_legs.how: knight per-kind max x 1.25, never under 8 deg/100ms

ang_speed_torso.how: knight per-kind max x 1.25, never under 8 deg/100ms

ang_speed_weapon.how: knight per-kind max x 1.25, never under 8 deg/100ms

foot_slide.how: knight per-kind max + 0.05 blocks (the booth's foot slide margin)

edge_lead.how: knight max over its slash attacks + 10 deg

loop_pose.how: knight per-kind max over its looping clips + 1 deg

loop_pos.how: knight per-kind max over its looping clips + 0.25 px

loop_vel.how: the limit is a ratio: a bone's wrap kink may be at most (knight per-kind max of kink / that bone's peak 1-tick speed in the clip) x 1.25 times its own peak speed, and never less than 8 deg/tick (a ~4 deg pop: under 1 px at the end of a 12 px limb)

elbow_bend.reason: the draw (volley, and the aim stances that hold it) folds the string arm until the hand is at the cheek (~130-145 deg), which a sword never does

ang_speed_arms.reason: the volley's draw and release snap the string arm back and out faster than the knight's cuts

elbow_bend.reason: spanning the crossbow folds the arm to haul the string back to the nut
the spear wall couches the shaft high at the shoulder, the rear elbow folded behind it

ang_speed_legs.reason: the high thrust is a lunge: the lead leg drives the point forward, which the knight's planted cuts never do

elbow_bend.reason: the harpoon is carried cocked above the shoulder, the throwing elbow folded

ang_speed_arms.reason: an overarm throw whips the arm faster than any melee swing
